# Introduction
```{r}
#| include: false
source("setup.R")
```

Aim: To determine how crickets ionoregulate during desiccation.

Crickets were placed in incubator in glass fly vials filled with ~1 inch of Drierite separated from the cricket by a cotton ball, stoppered with a sponge bung.

## Hypothesis

H0: Homoeostasis hypothesis: Ion concentration is regulated under desiccating conditions. Potential mechanisms include supplementation of water to maintain haemolymph volume or sequestration of ion to maintain concentration.

H1: No homeostasis hypothesis: Ion concentration increases proportionally with water loss because haemolymph volume decreases.   

## Design
```{r}
righty <- read_csv("data/Desiccation 2025/Ions/Potassium/righty_log_from_20251015_to_20251023_.csv")
names(righty) <- c("Time", "Temp", "RH", "MAC")
# Temperature
summary(righty$Temp)
```

Species: *Acheta domesticus*  
Time: 0, 3, 6, 18 or 24 (rehydrated) hours. Rehydrated crickets were dried for 18 hours then provided water for 6 hours.  
Temperature: `r round(mean(righty$Temp), 1)`&deg;C  
Sex: Male (blue) or Female (orange)

## Variables
Calculate mass in mg from grams:

  * Start mass: Mass at the start of the experiment
  * End mass: Mass after desiccation
  * Rehydrated mass: Mass after rehydration
  * Dry mass: Mass after drying in a oven at 60 &deg;C for at least 48 hours
  
Calculate change in mass between time points:

  * Percentage change in wet mass during desiccation
  * Percentage change in wet mass from start to end of rehydration
  
Calculate body water content from dry mass:

  * Total water content (%): All fluid in body relative to starting mass
  * Relative water loss (%): Body fluid lost during desiccation. Relative to total water content 
  
Calculate water loss rates:

  * Mass change rate (%/h): Percentage rate change during desiccation based on wet mass 
  * Water loss rate; WLR (%/h): Rate of relative water loss during desiccation 
  
```{r}
# LOAD AND PREPARE
drying_data_all <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/Ions/IonsData.xlsx")[1:15]
names(drying_data_all)[11] <- "Ion_conc"
drying_data_all$Ion <- ifelse(drying_data_all$Ion == "Na+", "Na+", "K+") # Relabel all potassium for consistency

# QUALITY CONTROL
# Remove poor readings and melanised samples
drying_data_all <- drying_data_all %>% 
  filter(`Read quality` != "Poor", 
         (!`Comment(s)` %in% c("Black","blackened", "Dead before")) %>% replace_na(TRUE)) 

# Calculate average conc across multiple readings for each ID
drying_data <- drying_data_all %>% 
  group_by(Ion, Cricket_ID, Sex, Time) %>% 
  summarise(Ion_conc = mean(Ion_conc)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Load mass data
mass_data <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/Ions/IonsData.xlsx", sheet = "mass") %>% 
  mutate(Desiccation_time = ifelse(Time == 24, 18, Time))
# Starting mass
mass_data$Start_mass <- (mass_data$Start.Cricket - mass_data$Start.Container) * 1000
# Mass after dehydration
mass_data$End_mass <- (mass_data$End.Cricket - mass_data$End.Container) * 1000
# Mass after rehydration
mass_data$Rehydrated_mass <- (mass_data$Rehydrated.Cricket - mass_data$Rehydrated.Container) * 1000

# Remove outlier sodium females (reasons discussed below)
mass_data <- filter(mass_data, !Cricket_ID  %in% c(334, 399, 441))

# Calculate wet mass metrics (mg)
# Relative change in dehydrated mass to starting mass
mass_data$Percent_change <- ifelse(mass_data$Time == 0, NA, 100 - (mass_data$End_mass / mass_data$Start_mass) * 100)
# Relative change in rehydrated mass to starting mass
mass_data$Percent_change_recovery <- ifelse(mass_data$Time == 24, (mass_data$Rehydrated_mass / mass_data$Start_mass) * 100, NA)

# Calculate dry mass metrics
# Total body water (mg)
mass_data$Body_water <- mass_data$Start_mass - mass_data$Dry_mass_mg
mass_data$Lost_water <- mass_data$Start_mass - mass_data$End_mass
# Total body water (%)
mass_data$Total_water_content <- ((mass_data$Start_mass - mass_data$Dry_mass_mg) / mass_data$Start_mass) * 100
# Water lost during desiccation (%)
mass_data$Relative_water_loss <- (mass_data$Percent_change /  mass_data$Total_water_content) * 100

# Merge and transform data
drying_data <- left_join(mass_data[,-c(4:9)], drying_data, by = c("Cricket_ID", "Sex", "Time"))

# Extract dead crickets
# dead_crickets <- filter(drying_data, is.na(Ion_conc))

drying_data <- drying_data %>% 
  drop_na(Ion_conc) %>% 
  # Exclude individuals that did not have ion concentration measured
  mutate(Time_fct = factor(Time, levels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "24")),
         log_ion = log10(Ion_conc),
         log_PC = log10(Percent_change)) 
```

### Cleaning data

Causes of exclusion:

* Death at any time; the time of death is unknown and mass could be overestimated.
* Dying - tended to have insufficient haemolymph. Alive and responsive but lethargic and with splayed legs indicating muscle issues (hyperkalemia?).
* Insufficient haemolymph; alive and responsive and not lethargic but haemocoel was empty.
* Poor quality readings; drifting electrode with no stable reading for 10 seconds
* Sample heavily melanised. Sodium is sensitive to melanisation (increases). Potassium concentration is stable over time.

K+:

* One male was excluded with >100 mM K^+^, this is a valid datapoint and measured multiple times.
* Cricket 434 died at the start of the experiment, haemolymph was sampled and frozen and had ions measured but theses are excluded from analysis. [K^+^] was higher than other crickets >100 mM K^+^
* 201 crickets measured

Na+:

* Cricket 350 was measured with a good read on a dodgy electrode but has abnormally low sodium. Was removed.
* Cricket 441 was measured with a good read but has abnormally low sodium. Was removed.
* Cricket 334 was injured in the vial. Leg fell off. Had abnormally high water loss and high sodium. Removed from analysis.
* Cricket 399 had abnormally high water loss and high sodium. Removed from analysis.
* 193 crickets measured

Checking distributions:

* K^+^ concentration is right skewed, still right skewed after Log 10 transformation but transformed.
* Na^+^ concentration is not skewed, Log 10 transformed anyway.
* Mass percent change is right skewed. Normally distributed after Log 10 transformation.
* Water loss rate is right skewed. More normally distributed after Log 10 transformation.

***

# Ion concentration

* Overall crickets are good regulators; magnitude of concentration changes are small
* Sex differences; females have higher concentrations of potassium and similar concentrations of sodium to males
* Variation around the mean is smaller in sodium. Variation in potassium is high in females. 
* Potassium does not change with longer desiccation or rehydration
* Sodium increases in females then returns to baseline levels after rehydration
* Sodium in males increases then returns to baseline levels after rehydration

**Conclusion:**  
Haemolymph potassium and sodium is being regulated. Females are better regulators than males. Males appear to under-compensate under short term desiccation; sodium increases at 3 hours but decreases under longer stress.

## Calculate mean and standard error
```{r}
mean_ion_conc <- drying_data %>% 
  group_by(Ion, Sex, Time) %>% 
  summarise(mean_conc = mean(Ion_conc),
            se_conc = sd(Ion_conc) / sqrt(n()),
            range = max(Ion_conc) - min(Ion_conc),
            n = n())
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(mean_ion_conc, digits = 3)
```


## Does ion concentration change over time?
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Potassium concentration (mM) for males (blue) and females (orange) does not increase with longer desiccation. Females have higher potassium concentration than males. Error bars are standard error around the mean."

p_potassium <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = filter(drying_data, Ion == "K+"), aes(Time, Ion_conc, colour = Sex), alpha = 0.6, stroke = NA,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0, jitter.width = 0.1, dodge = 1.5)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(mean_ion_conc, Ion == "K+"), aes(Time, mean_conc, group = Sex, colour = Sex),
             size = 2, shape = 1, show.legend = FALSE,
             position = position_dodge(0)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(mean_ion_conc, Ion == "K+"), aes(Time, mean_conc, group = Sex, colour = Sex),
                position = position_dodge(0), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = filter(mean_ion_conc, Ion == "K+"), aes(Time, group = Sex, colour = Sex,
                                      ymin = mean_conc - se_conc, 
                                      ymax = mean_conc + se_conc), 
                width = 1, linewidth = 0.5,
                position = position_dodge(0)) +
  labs(y = expression("[K"^"+"*"]" ~ ("mmol"%.%"L"^-1))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(3, 50), breaks = c(5, seq(10, 50, 10)), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time (h)", breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 18, 24), labels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "18 h + \n6 h recovery"))

p_potassium
```

### Stats

Count time as a continuous variable. Use categorical for HSD.

Potassium:

No interaction. 

```{r}
# Potassium
drying_data %>% 
  filter(Ion == "K+") %>%
  lm(log_ion ~ Time + Sex, .) %>% 
  anova() %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

drying_data %>% 
  filter(Ion == "K+") %>%
  lm(log_ion ~ Time_fct + Sex, .) %>% 
  anova()

pairs(emmeans(lm(log_ion ~ Time_fct * Sex, filter(drying_data, Ion == "K+")), ~ Time_fct * Sex), simple = "Time_fct", adjust = "Tukey")  
```

Interaction present.

## Does ion concentration change proportionally with mass lost?

H0: If crickets are not maintaining homeostasis, then ion concentration should increase proportionally with water lost during desiccation. Indicating that haemolymph is concentrating in the haemocoel. Slopes should be the same as 1 and different to 0.

H1: If crickets are maintaining homeostasis, then ion concentration should not have a relationship with water lost. Slopes should be similar to 0 or different to 1.

**Conclusion:**  
Haemolymph potassium is being regulated. Slopes are not different to 0 and different to 1.
Crickets are not regulating sodium. Slope is different to 0 and different to 1. Thus, sodium concentration is not proportional to amount of water lost during desiccation.

### Potassium:
```{r}
# Potassium equation
# Interaction term non-significant, dropped from model.
Kmass_data <- drying_data %>% 
  filter(Ion == "K+",
         !Time %in% c("0", "24")) %>% 
  mutate(ln_waterloss = log(Relative_water_loss),
         ln_ion = log(Ion_conc))

Kmass_mod <- lm(ln_ion ~ ln_waterloss, Kmass_data)
summary(Kmass_mod)

summary(lm((ln_ion-ln_waterloss) ~ ln_waterloss, Kmass_data)) # Slope is non-significant
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Potassium concentration (mM) against relative water loss (%). Females are orange. Males are blue. Potassium concentration is independent of mass lost for both sexes."
#| 
p_KWL <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = drying_data[!drying_data$Time %in% c("0", "24") & drying_data$Ion == "K+",], aes(Relative_water_loss, Ion_conc, colour = Sex), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(colour = "black", linewidth = 1, slope = coef(Kmass_mod)[2], intercept = coef(Kmass_mod)[1]) +
  labs(y = expression("[K"^"+"*"]" ~ ("mmol"%.%"L"^-1)),
       x = "Water lost (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log", limits = c(3, 50), breaks = c(5, seq(0, 150, 10)), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log", limits = c(1, 40), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0)), labels = function(x) round(x, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) 

p_KWL
```

### Sodium:
Slope is not equal to 1 but different to 0.
```{r}
Namass_data <- drying_data %>% 
  filter(Ion == "Na+",
         !Time %in% c("0", "24")) %>% 
  mutate(ln_waterloss = log(Relative_water_loss),
         ln_ion = log(Ion_conc))

Namass_mod <- lm(ln_ion ~ ln_waterloss, Namass_data)
summary(Namass_mod)

summary(lm((ln_ion-ln_waterloss) ~ ln_waterloss, Namass_data)) # Slope is non-significant

emtrends(Namass_mod, ~1, var = "ln_waterloss") %>% 
  test(., null = 1)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Sodium concentration (mM) against relative water loss (%). Females are orange. Males are blue. Both sexes increase sodium concentration with increasing water loss. "
#| 
p_NaWL <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = drying_data[!drying_data$Time %in% c("0", "24") & drying_data$Ion == "Na+",], aes(Relative_water_loss, Ion_conc, colour = Sex), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(colour = "black", linewidth = 1, slope = coef(Namass_mod)[2], intercept = coef(Namass_mod)[1]) +
  labs(y = expression("[Na"^"+"*"]" ~ ("mmol"%.%"L"^-1)),
       x = "Water lost (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log", limits = c(1, 40), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0)), labels = function(x) round(x, 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log", limits = c(130, 220), breaks = seq(100, 300, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) 
p_NaWL

```

# Relative change during desiccation

Mass lost is not expected to be linear because osmotic pressure will cause water to be increasingly harder to lose. Therefore, data was analysed assuming a power function and time and mass lost are log transformed.


```{r}
# Percentage change (wet mass)
mean_pc_loss <- drying_data %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  group_by(Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  summarise(mean_pc = mean(Percent_change),
            se_pc = sd(Percent_change) / sqrt(n()),
            range = max(Percent_change) - min(Percent_change),
            n = n()) 

knitr::kable(mean_pc_loss, digits = 3)
```

There was no interaction between sex and time so the interaction term was dropped from the model.

```{r}
PC_mod <- drying_data %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  lm(log(Percent_change) ~ log(Desiccation_time) + Sex, .) 

PC_fit <- drying_data %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  select(Desiccation_time, Sex) %>% 
  cbind(., exp(predict(PC_mod, newdata = ., interval = "prediction")))

summary(PC_mod)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Wet mass lost (%) of female (orange) and male (blue) crickets during desiccation. Data from potassium and sodium are pooled. Lines are a fitted power function. Males lose more mass than females at all time points. Error bars are standard error around the mean."

p_wetmass <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = drying_data %>% 
               filter(!Time %in% c("0")), aes(Desiccation_time, Percent_change, colour = Sex), alpha = 0.6, 
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0, jitter.width = 0.1, dodge = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(data = mean_pc_loss, aes(Desiccation_time, mean_pc, colour = Sex), 
              size = 2, shape = 16,
             position = position_dodge(1)) +
  geom_errorbar(data = mean_pc_loss, aes(Desiccation_time, colour = Sex,
                                            ymin = mean_pc - se_pc,
                                            ymax = mean_pc + se_pc),
                width = 1, linewidth = 1,
             position = position_dodge(1)) +
  geom_line(data = PC_fit, aes(Desiccation_time, fit, colour = Sex), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(y = "Wet mass lost (%)",
       x = "Desiccation time (h)") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 35, 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 18))

p_wetmass
```

## Percentage change in mass

18 hours of desiccation is borderline where mortality occurs. Individuals that lose more than 30% of their starting mass are dead or dying. This is more likely in males than females and appears random in males; males of all sizes can lose extreme body mass. Fewer occurrences in females but those that did were smaller females.

## Rehydration
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Change in mass (%) of crickets before and after desiccation and rehydration relative to their starting mass."

rehydration_ions <- mass_data %>% 
  filter(Time == 24,
         Survival == 1) %>% 
  select(Cricket_ID, Sex, Percent_change, Percent_change_recovery) %>% 
  mutate(Start_Percent = 100,
         Percent_change = 100 - Percent_change) %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("Percent"), names_to = "Timepoint", values_to = "Change") %>% 
  mutate(Experiment = "Ions", 
         Time_treatment = "24_starved",
         Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Start_Percent", "Percent_change", "Percent_change_recovery"))) 

ggplot(rehydration_ions, aes(Timepoint, Change, group = Cricket_ID)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  ylab("Relative mass change (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 120, 5), limits = c(70, 105), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point", labels = c("Pre-desiccation", "Post-desiccation", "Post-recovery")) +
  facet_grid(~Sex)

save(mass_data, drying_data, rehydration_ions, file = "data/Desiccation 2025/ions.Rdata")
```

## Survival curve

Losses of 45% are lethal.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "How much relative water loss (%) can a cricket tolerate before increasing the risk of mortality?"
#| fig-height: 5
surv_mod <- glm(Survival ~ Relative_water_loss, mass_data, family = "binomial")
surv_fit <- data.frame(Relative_water_loss = seq(0, max(mass_data$Relative_water_loss, na.rm = TRUE)), Survival = predict(surv_mod, newdata = data.frame(Relative_water_loss = seq(0, max(mass_data$Relative_water_loss, na.rm = TRUE))), type = "response"))

log(0.5/(1-0.5)) - coef(surv_mod)[1] /coef(surv_mod)[2]

surv_plot <- ggplot(mass_data, aes(Relative_water_loss, Survival), mass_data) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = surv_fit, aes(Relative_water_loss, Survival)) +
  annotate(x = log(0.5/(1-0.5)) - coef(surv_mod)[1] /coef(surv_mod)[2],
           y = 0, yend = 0.5, geom = "segment", linetype = 2) +
  annotate(xend = log(0.5/(1-0.5)) - coef(surv_mod)[1] /coef(surv_mod)[2],
           x = 0, y = 0.5, geom = "segment", linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 80), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 6, r = 10, b = 6, l = 6, unit = "pt")) +
  labs(y = "Probability of survival",
       x = "Relative water loss (%)") 
  
surv_plot

ggsave(surv_plot, dpi = 300, width = ppt_width, units = "mm", height = ppt_height, filename = "data/Desiccation 2025/figures/ion_survival.png")
```

ggsave(p_ions, dpi = 300, width = single_width, units = "mm", height = 170, filename = "data/Desiccation 2025/figures/Fig2ion_con.png")

p_ionmass <- p_KWL +
  p_NaWL +
  plot_layout(axis_titles = "collect" , guides =
                "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title.position = "left")
ggsave(p_ionmass, dpi = 300, width = double_width, units = "mm", height = single_height, filename = "data/Desiccation 2025/figures/FigS1ion_mass.png")
